verbalization: Pralatrexate is associated with the development of Primary Cutaneous Aggressive Epidermotropic Cd8+ T-cell Lymphoma through a pathway involving Forodesine. The evidence suggests that Pralatrexate, which is indicated for Primary Cutaneous Gamma/delta-positive T-cell Lymphoma and Primary Cutaneous Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma Not Otherwise Specified, may act as a mediator in the progression of the more aggressive form of the disease. The shared indication for Forodesine in both pathways implies a potential role for Forodesine in the pathogenesis of this lymphoma, possibly through a common mechanism involving T-cell activation or proliferation. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible link between Pralatrexate and the lymphoma through a shared therapeutic target or pathway, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
